title: Getting Started on Your Project
author: Bonnie L Hurwitz
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jqrcmv6

steps.title: Log into HPC and ocelote cluster
steps.instruction:
Open a terminal and connect to the high‑performance computing system, then SSH to the ocelote cluster using the commands:
```
ssh hpcocelote
ssh hpc ocelote
```

steps.title: Create class project directory
steps.instruction:
Make a directory for the class project, replacing **username** with your own user name:
```
mkdir /rsgrps/bh_class/username
```

steps.title: Enter user directory
steps.instruction:
Change into the directory you just created:
```
cd /rsgrps/bh_class/username
```

steps.title: Create FASTQ download directories
steps.instruction:
Create two directories for the FASTQ files and move into one of them:
```
mkdir fastqcd fastq
mkdir fastq
cd fastq
```

steps.title: Create SRR list file
steps.instruction:
Create a plain‑text file named **list** that contains all SRR accession numbers (one per line) using nano:
```
nano list
```

steps.title: Create get‑fastq.sh script with PBS directives
steps.instruction:
Edit a new file called **get‑fastq.sh** (e.g., with nano) and paste the exact script below, preserving every line and spacing:
```
#!/bin/bash
#PBS -W group_list=bh_class
#PBS -q standard
#PBS -l select=9:ncpus=28:mem=27gb
#PBS -l pvmem=235gb
#PBS -l walltime=48:00:00
#PBS -l cput=48:00:00
#PBS -M username@email.arizona.edu
#PBS -m bea
module load sratools
echo "my job_id is: ${PBS_JOBID}"
FASTQ_DIR="/rsgrps/bh_class/username/fastq"
export FASTQ_DIR
cd $FASTQ_DIR
for file in `cat list`; do
  fastq-dump --outdir $FASTQ_DIR \
    --gzip --skip-technical --readids --dumpbase \
    --split-files --clip $file;
 done
```

steps.title: Make get‑fastq.sh executable
steps.instruction:
Create the script file (if not already present) and set execute permissions, as shown in the original text (the commands are repeated in the source):
```
touch get-fastq.sh
chmod 755 get-fastq.sh
touch get-fastq.sh
chmod 755 get-fastq.sh
```

steps.title: Check job status
steps.instruction:
Use the qstat command to see whether the job is still running. The original example filters the output with egrep and the job ID:
```
qstat
qstat | egrep hur815336.head1
```
